title: Regression Sentinel: Multi-GPU Tensor+Pipeline Parallel Throughput Probe
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reproducible harness (a `sentinel`) that continuously exercises multi-GPU distributed inference paths (tensor parallelism + pipeline parallelism) to measure sustained tokens/sec and p95 latency, detect regressions automatically, and surface low-noise alerts to the Console and PagerDuty.

Why: Recent rollouts of kernel selection and KV-cache optimizations produced occasional regressions on TGX clusters when TP/PP splits change. Current nightly suites exercise correctness and single-run throughput, but we lack a lightweight continuous probe that mirrors production mix (mixed prompt lengths, short tail latency) and triggers statistical alerts for regressions in tokens/sec or p95.

Scope and success criteria:
- Implement harness that runs on dedicated perf-cluster, exercising representative model variants (gpt-6B/13B/70B equiv) with TP/PP configurations used in Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Primary metrics: sustained tokens/sec (1m rolling), p95 generation latency (per-request), error rate, KV-cache hit ratio. Store time-series to TSDB and export to Console.
- Regression detection: automatic daily baseline comparison using rolling-window median and an outlier detector (CUSUM + robust z-score). Alert if sustained tokens/sec drops >7% for 30+ minutes OR p95 increases >15% with p<0.01.
- Low-flapping alerting: require 3 consecutive windows (10m windows) and a minimum sample size before firing.
- End-to-end pipeline: harness -> metrics -> regression engine -> Console dashboard + Alert rule + Slack/PagerDuty integration.
- Acceptance: alerts validated by SRE on two injected regressions; dashboard shows historical rollups and RL (regression likelihood) metric.

Bench plan and workload shapes:
- Hardware: 8xA100-80GB and homogeneous 4xH100-80GB pool for comparison. Use existing infra labels: `perf-mgpu-a100-8`, `perf-h100-4`.
- TP/PP shapes to run: [TP=2,PP=2], [TP=4,PP=1], [TP=8,PP=1], [TP=1,PP=4] to cover common splits.
- Batch strategies: continuous batching with batch_max_tokens=8192, dynamic batching off/on permutations.
- Prompt mixes:
  - Short: 512 tokens (60% of requests)
  - Medium: 1024 tokens (30%)
  - Long: 2048 tokens (10%)
- QPS target per-shape to saturate pipeline: derived from model flops table; initial target 25k tokens/sec aggregate per 8-GPU cluster.
- Warm-up: each run warms KV-cache with 10k tokens then measures for 60 minutes per configuration.

Measurement methodology:
- Measure tokens/sec as total tokens emitted / wall-clock active time (exclude warm-up windows).
- Per-request latencies: measure generation end-to-end and compute p50/p90/p95/p99.
- Use bootstrapped confidence intervals for tokens/sec and p95.
- Store raw traces and per-token timestamps to S3 for postmortem if regression triggers.

Regression detection algorithm:
- Baseline window: trailing 7 days of harness runs grouped by shape and hardware.
- Compute median tokens/sec and median absolute deviation (MAD) for robustness.
- CUSUM over minute-level tokens/sec to detect gradual drift; robust z-score on p95 to detect spikes.
- Thresholds configurable by release/shape. Default thresholds: tokens/sec drop >7% sustained 30min, p95 increase >15% absolute.
- Alert metadata includes affected shape, hw pool, run id, recent PRs (if rollouts detected), and link to stored traces.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We will implement harness as a Go microservice that can be scheduled as a Kubernetes CronJob and also as a long-running Deployment. Rationale: low overhead, easy integration with existing runtime clients.
- Use existing runtime client test harness to replay requests; add a lightweight traffic marshaller that injects KV-cache warmups and measures per-token timing.
- To reduce noise, runs will pin cgroups to avoid multi-tenant interference and tag nodes with `perf-reserved` label.
- Regression engine initially runs offline (air-gapped script) and posts findings to metrics/alerts; later we will migrate it into the Console backend for real-time alerts.

Artifacts and links:
- Perf harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-sentinels/pull/142 (draft)
- Dashboard (Console): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/perf/regression-sentinel (beta)
- Raw traces and results: s3://redwood-perf/sentinels/ENG-48921/2026-03-12/
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Distributed+Regression+Sentinel

Risks and mitigation:
- Flaky noisy measurements from shared infra -> mitigate by dedicated nodes and sampling.
- False positives during autoscaler activity -> label measurements with scaling events and exclude windows overlapping autoscaler spikes.
- Large storage cost for raw per-token timestamps -> keep 14-day retention for raw traces, aggregate to 90 days.

Next steps:
1) Merge initial harness PR and deploy to `perf-mgpu-a100-8` as a Canary (Daniel) — target 2026-03-18.
2) Run 2-week baseline to collect rolling stats and tune thresholds (Aisha + SRE).
3) Wire regression outputs into Console alerts and create PagerDuty escalation policy (SRE).
4) Postmortem and playbook for reacting to regression alerts.

Acceptance criteria checklist:
- [ ] Harness merged and running on two hw pools for >=72 hours
- [ ] Console dashboard shows stable tokens/sec and p95 series for each TP/PP shape
- [ ] Regression detector flags two injected regressions in controlled test with correct metadata
- [ ] Alert routing to Slack + PagerDuty verified
